title: Lump-Sum Settlement of a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Deficiency
content:
**Customer terms and desk reference — settling a deficiency on a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract**

A deficiency left after a repossessed vehicle is sold may be settled by the customer with a single lump-sum payment that pays the contract in full. The desk states one settlement figure, worked out under the settlement terms of the Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, and an offer below that figure is not within the servicing desk's authority.

**Prerequisite.** The settlement figure is fixed only after a deficiency quote dated the settlement date stands on the account. Equivalently: while no deficiency quote dated the settlement date stands on the account, no settlement figure is fixed.

### Paying the settlement

For a settlement payment, and only for such a payment, the customer sends it by bank wire from the customer's own bank account, a certified-funds channel that is accepted while the contract takes certified funds only, and the wire is credited when it is received, whatever the hour: a wire sent on a Monday through Friday posts the same day, and one sent on a Saturday or a Sunday posts on the Monday that follows; a settlement is not taken on a US federal holiday or on a Saturday or Sunday before a Monday that is one.

Every payment other than a deficiency settlement wire or reinstatement funds, both of which post on the day they are received or on the Monday after a weekend as the settlement and reinstatement terms state, keeps the standard posting: one received before the payment cutoff time Central Time on a business day posts that day, and one received later, or on a weekend or US federal holiday, posts the next business day.

The settlement is applied on its posting date as every payment is, first to the simple interest accrued since the interest-paid-to date, then to principal until the past-due amount is satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal; once it posts the contract is paid in full and whatever principal and fees remain are closed.

| Wire sent on | Posts on |
|---|---|
| Monday through Friday (not a US federal holiday) | the same day, whatever the hour |
| Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday not a holiday | the following Monday |
| A US federal holiday, or a weekend day before a Monday holiday | not taken |

### The customer's payment: `remit_deficiency_settlement_2e6b8900`

This tool belongs to the customer. The agent unlocks `remit_deficiency_settlement_2e6b8900` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to pay the settlement from the customer's own bank account by bank wire transfer.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `preowned_contract_id` | the reference number of the customer's pre-owned contract, as given to the customer by the servicing agent from the contract lookup | identifier |
| `amount` | the settlement amount in US dollars, exactly as the agent states it | a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half-up to the cent |
| `funding_account_last4` | the last four digits of the bank account the payment is drawn from, as printed on the customer's own bank records | 4 digits; never empty for this payment |

**Effect.** On success one settlement payment is posted to the contract for the stated amount, dated with the posting date (the day the wire is sent, or the Monday when it is sent on a Saturday or Sunday), split in the contract's payment allocation order into the simple interest accrued through the posting date, principal and fees due; the contract is marked paid in full as of the posting date, with the principal and fees due it no longer owes closed to zero.

**Return.** A confirmation naming the payment reference (an opaque id beginning with "ppm_"), the contract reference, the amount paid in US dollars with 2 decimals, the interest, principal and fees portions in US dollars with 2 decimals, the channel "wire", the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD), the funding account's last four digits and the contract status `paid_in_full`. The presence of the payment reference shows the payment posted.
